bridge: Builds on S06 identity, F03 sandboxing and G02 privacy. This is a survey with one concrete permission exercise; advanced platform engineering requires the linked specialist material.
teaching:
Foreground access happens while a person is actively using the relevant app feature; background access continues when that feature is not actively in use, under platform rules. An exported interface is an app entry point other apps may be able to call. A deep link is a URL-like input that opens a particular app screen or operation. Treat those inputs as requests to validate, not trusted instructions simply because the app opened.

Mobile platforms mediate app access through sandbox, permission, signing and distribution systems. A permission prompt is one layer: the app still needs a legitimate purpose, safe data handling and server-side authorisation. A signed package identifies a signing relationship, not a universal guarantee of benign behaviour.

Compare foreground access, background access and exported inter-app interfaces under the chosen platform's current rules. Those rules evolve, so use official documentation for exact API/version behaviour. Deep links and app-to-app messages create input boundaries similar to web requests.

The exercise in this lesson focuses on minimising data access for an invented note app. No phone rooting, malware installation or private data extraction is required. State what remains outside the survey: native code auditing, platform exploit development and complete store-compliance review need additional specialised study.

An SDK linked into an app commonly runs with that app’s authority; an OS permission cannot distinguish two pieces of code inside the same principal automatically. Review what third-party code receives, not only the prompt text. Distinguish the developer upload key from the distributed app-signing key when Play App Signing is used. Mainline updates selected modular system components through documented channels; it neither updates every vendor component nor makes every device eligible indefinitely. Record the exact device, platform version, security patch level and vendor support policy before assessing update coverage.

The older Android lecture illustrates an isolation boundary, not the complete current platform. An application can contain native code and can use multiple processes; being written in Java is not its sandbox. Modern application isolation combines Linux identities with additional platform controls. Sharing an app process or embedding an SDK can share substantial authority. For an actual app, inspect the current target version, exported components, permissions and data flows using the official platform documentation.
example:
Fictional offline notes app
Required function: write/read local text notes.
Proposed permissions: camera, microphone, contacts, precise location, network.
No feature uses these capabilities.
Decision: request none of them for the stated function.
If a later scan feature is added: request camera only when invoked,
explain purpose and retain a manual-entry path where feasible.
explanation: Permission need follows the feature and platform contract. “We might use it later” is not sufficient justification. A denied optional permission should not break unrelated note reading. Server data access remains separately scoped to the signed-in account.
exercise: Create a capability/purpose table for the app. Add a photo-attachment feature and define when access is requested, what data is retained and what happens after denial. Use the current official platform guide before claiming exact prompt behaviour.
solution: For the stated offline text-note function, camera, microphone, contacts, precise location and network have no supplied purpose, so the capability table rejects each. For optional photo attachment, offer the platform-supported selection interface when the learner chooses Attach photo, explain the attachment purpose, retain only the selected image under the stated local storage/deletion design, and leave note reading/writing available if selection is cancelled or access denied. Android’s official Photo Picker guide describes a selection route without broad library access; exact availability, fallback and APIs depend on platform/library versions. This paper design is not evidence that a built app implements those choices.
challenge: An exported deep link accepts note_id and account_id from another app. Explain the trust boundary and design checks preventing access to another user's note.
challenge_solution: Treat both fields as untrusted input; derive account identity from trusted session/platform state and authorise the target object. App signing and a valid link format do not prove the caller may select an arbitrary account.
